strategy.summary: Stryker left 6 mutants alive in src/pricing.js because the tests skip boundary values and two applyCoupon tests have no real assertion. The plan adds exact-value assertions to those two tests and adds cases at the $50 shipping boundary, at exactly $100 with SAVE20, and for an orderTotal that includes shipping. The expected values come from the README and JSDoc, which agree with the code.
inScope: applyCoupon, shippingCost and orderTotal behaviour in src/pricing.js at the points the 6 surviving mutants change
outOfScope: The 2 mutants that no test reaches (missing coverage, which the work item excludes)
Restructuring the existing tests beyond adding assertions and cases
assumptions: README and JSDoc state the intended behaviour: free shipping at a subtotal >= $50, SAVE20 only applies when the subtotal is strictly over $100, and the total is the discounted subtotal plus shipping
Existing tests keep their titles and what they cover; in TC2, toBeDefined is replaced by the stricter toBe(50), which still fails whenever toBeDefined would

risks.description: Off-by-one at the coupon and shipping thresholds would go unnoticed and customers would be charged the wrong amount
risks.mitigation: Add tests that use the exact boundary inputs, 50 and 100

acceptanceCriteria.text: Shipping is free for a subtotal of exactly $50 or more
A code other than SAVE20, or no code, leaves the subtotal unchanged
SAVE20 leaves a subtotal of $100 or less unchanged
orderTotal adds shipping to the discounted subtotal when shipping is charged

testCases.title: handles an order without a coupon
testCases.rationale: Strengthens the existing test, which asserts nothing. Kills mutant 1 (code check → true) and mutant 2 (&& → ||): with either change a 200 order with no code is discounted to 160.

testCases.title: handles a small order with the coupon
testCases.rationale: Replaces toBeDefined with the exact value. Kills mutant 4 (subtotal > 100 → true) and mutant 2 (&& → ||), which both discount 50 to 40.

testCases.title: does not discount an order of exactly 100 with SAVE20
testCases.rationale: Kills mutant 5 (> 100 → >= 100), which would discount the boundary order to 80.

testCases.title: ships an order of exactly 50 for free
testCases.rationale: Kills mutant 3 (>= 50 → > 50), which would charge 4.99 at exactly $50.

testCases.title: adds shipping to a small order's total
testCases.rationale: Kills mutant 6 (+ shipping → - shipping), which would give 15.01. The existing orderTotal test has free shipping, so + and - give the same result there.

strategy.environmentNotes: None; pure unit tests run with `npm test` (vitest).
